daily_brief: Diplomatic momentum on Ukraine accelerated Friday as the Kremlin announced trilateral peace talks with the US and Ukraine are scheduled for early November in Abu Dhabi [The Hindu, BBC], though Kyiv reported continued Starlink connectivity issues affecting drone operations despite President Trump's claims that restrictions had been lifted [BBC]. Oil markets spiked to $114 per barrel amid reports the Trump administration is considering renewed strikes on Iran after the midterms [RNZ, Financial Times], while tech stocks suffered a significant sell-off on mounting concerns over AI-sector debt sustainability [Nikkei, Financial Times]. In France, authorities extended Paris curfews and banned protests in Lyon and Marseille ahead of expected weekend demonstrations, with President Macron labeling unauthorized protests 'illegitimate' following last weekend's widespread unrest [BBC, RFI]. West Africa faced a public health crisis as Nigeria confirmed an Ebola case in Abuja linked to travel from Congo, expanding an outbreak that has already reached Kenya [The Guardian]. Meanwhile, a BBC investigation documented 43 attacks on hospitals by Sudan's RSF during the siege of el-Fasher, with the UN human rights chief calling the findings evidence of potential war crimes [BBC].

top_stories.headline: Russia-Ukraine-US Peace Talks Scheduled for November in Abu Dhabi
bullets: Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov announced trilateral talks between Russia, Ukraine and the US are planned for early November in Abu Dhabi in a three-party format
The announcement followed meetings between US special envoy Steve Witkoff and both President Zelensky in Oslo and President Putin in St. Petersburg this week
Putin stated talks would focus on security arrangements for a final peace deal rather than a short truce; Russia suggested around November 10 as a target date
Ukraine called for discussions to happen 'as soon as possible' while both sides voiced readiness to resume direct talks mediated by Washington

sources.name: The Hindu
sources.framing_note: Detailed diplomatic timeline with quotes from multiple officials

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Emphasized strikes on Kyiv occurring hours after Russia agreed to talks, noting Zelensky's criticism of US envoy calling Putin a 'humanitarian'

top_stories.headline: Ukraine Reports Starlink Restrictions Persist Despite Trump's Claims of Restoration
bullets: Ukrainian defense ministry sources told the BBC that drones continue experiencing connection loss at speeds exceeding 161km/h (100mph), hampering military operations
President Trump initially denied instructing Elon Musk to restrict connectivity, then stated Thursday that Musk had 'put it back'
Musk previously claimed Starshield, used by Ukraine for some operations, is controlled by the US military and suggested the Pentagon could be responsible
Ukrainian officials said there is 'currently no confirmation that these restrictions have been lifted' as military monitoring continues

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Fact-focused reporting on conflicting claims between US officials and Ukrainian ground reports

top_stories.headline: Oil Prices Surge Past $113 on Reports US Considering Iran Strikes After Midterms
bullets: Brent crude rose 4% to over $113 per barrel, hitting its highest level since May; West Texas Intermediate climbed 3% to nearly $100
New York Times reported the Trump administration has drawn up plans for renewed strikes on Iran after November's US midterm elections
US ordered some non-emergency government staff to leave Saudi Arabia as Iran-backed Houthi rebels continue missile strikes on Saudi territory
Global oil prices peaked at $126 per barrel in April during the US-Iran war earlier this year

sources.name: RNZ
sources.framing_note: Included New Zealand domestic impact on petrol prices

sources.name: Financial Times
sources.framing_note: Linked oil surge to broader market concerns about AI sector debt

top_stories.headline: France Extends Curfews and Bans Protests Ahead of Expected Weekend Unrest
bullets: Paris extended partial curfews through Monday; Marseille and Lyon imposed total bans on protests this weekend after widespread rioting and looting
President Macron declared 'illegitimate' protests would be banned, blaming ultra-left groups and vandals for last weekend's violence
217 people have been jailed in fast-track trials; 2,700 arrested across France with over 1,000 appearing in court; half had no prior criminal record
Police deployments increased 20%; the Louvre, Orsay and Picasso museums will close Saturday; National Rally congress in Orléans expected to draw counter-protests of up to 25,000

sources.name: BBC Europe
sources.framing_note: Focused on security measures and arrest statistics

sources.name: RFI English
sources.framing_note: More detailed on political context, including 'rioters pay' legislation and National Rally congress

sources.name: France 24
sources.framing_note: Brief video coverage of shop owners bracing for unrest

top_stories.headline: BBC Investigation Documents Systematic RSF Attacks on Hospitals in Sudan's El-Fasher
bullets: BBC documented at least 43 separate attacks on hospitals and healthcare sites in el-Fasher from May 2024 to October 2025, some facilities hit multiple times
From April 2023 to October 2025, 120 medical workers were injured, 55 killed, and 10 forcibly disappeared or abducted
UN human rights chief Volker Türk called findings 'deeply disturbing,' stating attacks may amount to war crimes under international humanitarian law
RSF rejected the findings; the health minister of RSF's civilian-affiliated government dismissed allegations as propaganda to smear their reputation

sources.name: BBC World
sources.framing_note: Investigative report with detailed methodology and on-the-ground sources; included RSF denial and UN response
